structured_kernel_small.description: Deterministic (no RNG) p=3 trait x n=12 site fixture, reused VERBATIM from test/parity/fixtures/core070_structured_data.R's df/C/K2 construction (the same fixture cited by structured-required-case-plan.json's STRUCT-KER-SINGLE-PSI/STRUCT-KER-MULTI cases): expand.grid(site=1:12, trait=1:3), species = rep(rep(c('a','b','c'), each=4), 3) (3 species levels, 4 sites each), value = sin(row_index/3) + trait_int/5, C = .7*diag(3)+.3 (species x species kernel), K2 = .6*diag(3)+.4*tcrossprod(c(1,-1,1)) (both PD, dimnamed by species levels a,b,c).

cases.tolerance_note: Authoring-time calibration (contract never previously accepted, not a widening): this is the programme's FIRST curvature-level comparison — sigma_eps Wald CI endpoints from two INDEPENDENTLY fitted models whose SE machinery differs structurally (frozen R: TMB sdreport AD Hessian; Julia: observed-information Hessian in confint.jl). Measured endpoint gap on this fixture 2.06e-3 with point estimates agreeing at the 1e-4 paired-fit class; 5e-3 bounds the SE-machinery difference while still failing on any estimand/transform mismatch (which would show at ~1e-1). Recorded as first SE-level evidence, NOT an SE-parity claim.

GLLVM.extract_lv_effects(fit::GllvmFit; type=:trait_effect) exists and is exported (src/postfit.jl:353) but HARD-gates on _has_lv_predictor(fit) -- it throws ArgumentError unless the fit came from fit_gaussian_gllvm(...; X_lv=...) (a concurrent/constrained-ordination fit with a predictor-informed latent axis). None of this batch's reused fixtures (gaussian_small, structured_kernel_small) carry an X_lv predictor; gaussian_small is a plain unconstrained-latent fit, so calling extract_lv_effects(fit_g) would throw on the Julia side by design, and the presumed R equivalent (a num.lv.c concurrent-ordination gllvmTMB formula) was never fit either. Building and validating a dedicated X_lv/num.lv.c fixture pair (R + Julia) is a genuine new-fixture slice, out of this lean batch's reuse-only scope; left for a follow-up wave.

Julia surface extract_Gamma(fit::GllvmFit; row_traits, col_traits) already exists (src/extract_gamma.jl:36, exported) and is independently tested, so this is NOT a missing-Julia-surface case. It requires a Lambda_phy-bearing fit built via fit_gaussian_gllvm(Y; K_phy>0, Sigma_phy=K*) with K* from make_cross_kernel (a two-lineage cross-kernel construction) -- none of this batch's fixtures (structured_kernel_small, gaussian_small, or wave-5's twolevel_small/ordinal_small) carry a phylo/cross-kernel tier. Per formula-recognizer-spec.md Sec 1.5, the native Sigma_phy= route puts phylogeny on the TRAIT axis and is explicitly NOT the same model as any R gllvmTMB coevolution formula (docs/dev-log/core070/structured-native-mapping.md:49-56) -- confirmed independently here, matching the identical deferral already recorded in docs/dev-log/core070/surface-conversion-batch-contract.json's deferred[] for the same row in wave-5. No defensible R-paired numeric case exists without inventing and validating a dedicated coevolution fixture against a live R gllvmTMB coevolution fit, which is out of this batch's fixture-reuse scope.

No Julia deviance() function or dispatch exists anywhere in src/ for AnyGllvmFit/GllvmFit (grep -rn 'function.*deviance|deviance(fit' src/*.jl matches only confint_profile.jl's LOCAL closures deviance_lower/deviance_upper inside the profile-CI bracket-and-bisect routine, not a public StatsAPI.deviance method; deviance is also absent from src/GLLVM.jl's export list). Composing an ad hoc definition (e.g. -2*loglikelihood(fit) plus a saturated-model term) without reading R's actual deviance.gllvmTMB_multi source (not available in this Julia-only worktree) risks silently asserting the wrong estimand, which this repo's culture treats as worse than an honest defer. Left for a dedicated slice with R source access to confirm R's exact residual-deviance definition before any Julia composition is authored.
